Sudan has accused Ethiopia of allowing drone attacks against its territory and aiding the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which have been in conflict with the Sudanese Armed Forces since April 2023. In response, Sudan has lodged complaints with the UN Security Council and the African Union, while Ethiopia has expelled Sudanese diplomats and closed its consulate in Asosa. The situation is further complicated by longstanding disputes over the Fashaga border area and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which have historically strained relations. Analysts warn that these tensions could lead to military confrontations, potentially destabilizing the Horn of Africa. The overlapping conflicts and security concerns in both nations highlight the urgent need for diplomatic dialogue to prevent further escalation and ensure regional stability.

ethiopia.title: Ethiopia's Green Legacy Showcases Commitment to Global Climate Action - Pmo Press Secretary
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia's Green Legacy Showcases Commitment to Global Climate Action - Pmo Press Secretary - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia's Green Legacy Showcases Commitment to Global Climate Action - Pmo Press Secretary 13 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — The Green Legacy Initiative stands as a testament to Ethiopia's commitment to combating climate change through large-scale afforestation, environmental conservation and sustainable development, Press Secretary for Office of the Prime Minister (PMO) Billene Seyoum said. Speaking at a briefing on Ethiopia's participation in the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Billene highlighted the country's progress in environmental protection, renewable energy expansion and preparations to host COP32 in 2027. She disclosed that Ethiopia has planted more than 56 billion seedlings over the past eight years under the Green Legacy Initiative. The Press Secretary described this the flagship national programme as a major contribution to global efforts to mitigate climate change and restore degraded ecosystems. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Billene stressed, however, that the initiative's success should not be measured by the number of seedlings planted alone, but also by their survival, continued care and protection to ensure lasting environmental benefits. She called for broader public participation in environmental conservation, emphasizing that nurturing and protecting planted trees must become a shared responsibility across all sections of society. She also recalled Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's repeated calls for citizens to take an active role in caring for planted trees to maximize their long-term environmental and economic benefits. Turning to Ethiopia's clean energy transition, Billene highlighted the country's expanding investments in hydropower, wind and solar energy to meet growing domestic electricity demand while strengthening its capacity to supply power to regional markets. She cited ongoing wind and solar projects as evidence of Ethiopia's efforts to diversify its renewable energy mix and advance a sustainable energy future. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), she added, represents a major milestone in the country's renewable energy ambitions and electricity generation capacity. The landmark project will also be showcased at the Ethiopian Pavilion during COP31, she pointed out. Billene underscored that Ethiopia's investments in renewable energy, afforestation and environmental protection go beyond domestic development priorities, contributing to broader international efforts to address climate change and promote sustainable development. The briefing also highlighted Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's engagements at COP31, Ethiopia's preparations to host COP32 in 2027, and the country's plans to present its development achievements and climate action initiatives to the international community. The inhabitants further emphasized the need for consolidating progress toward lasting peace, stability and prosperity in the region. The call was made during a consultative forum of Mekelle residents, presided over by Chief of Staff of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF), Field Marshal Birhanu Jula. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Speaking at the gathering, Field Marshal Birhanu said the defunct TPLF faction had aligned itself with the so-called "Tsimdo" group, an alliance orchestrated by Ethiopia's historical adversaries to wage war against the country. He said his engagement with residents was aimed at fostering dialogue, strengthening cooperation and encouraging collective efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in Tigray region. During the discussions, residents underscored their strong desire to see an end to conflict, identifying peace, security and sustainable development as their foremost priorities. They called for the reconstruction of damaged infrastructure, expanded employment opportunities for young people and the restoration of security to enable communities to resume normal life without fear. "Our foremost priorities are the reconstruction of critical infrastructure, the creation of meaningful employment opportunities for our youth, and the restoration of security so that citizens can go about their daily lives in peace," participants said. Residents also welcomed the resumption of salary payments for civil servants and ongoing infrastructure rehabilitation efforts, describing them as important steps toward restoring normalcy and accelerating the region's recovery. Concluding the forum, participants called on the Federal Government to maintain its commitment to Tigray, sustain ongoing interventions and accelerate reform, reconstruction and development initiatives to secure lasting peace and improve the livelihoods of communities across the region. According to official statements from both governments, Erdoğan reaffirmed Türkiye's commitment to expanding cooperation with Ethiopia across multiple sectors and its continued support for peace and stability in the region. PM Abiy described the discussions as productive, saying the two leaders explored opportunities to deepen their existing partnership. "Building on the strong partnership between our two countries, we discussed opportunities to further strengthen bilateral cooperation," Abiy said. "This includes collaboration as Ethiopia prepares to assume the COP32 Presidency, as well as on regional issues of mutual interest." Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Türkiye's emphasis on regional peace comes against the backdrop of its mediation efforts to ease tensions between Ethiopia and Somalia following the January 2024 memorandum of understanding between Addis Abeba and Somaliland, which triggered a diplomatic fallout with Mogadishu. Erdoğan hosted Abiy and Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in Ankara on 11 December 2024, where the two leaders r eached the Ankara Declaration , reaffirming their commitment to each other's sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity. The declaration also recognized Ethiopia's interest in securing reliable access to the sea through arrangements negotiated with Somalia under its sovereign authority, with Türkiye facilitating subsequent technical negotiations. The Turkish Foreign Ministry described the agreement as a framework for translating the leaders' commitments into mutually beneficial cooperation. The talks in Antalya also come against the backdrop of expanding Turkish economic engagement in Ethiopia. Turkish investment in the country reached nearly $2.5 billion in the 2023/24 fiscal year, making Türkiye one of Ethiopia's top three investor countries. Turkish investments span construction, manufacturing, agriculture and the chemical industries. Beyond commercial investments, Türkiye has maintained humanitarian and development assistance programs in Ethiopia through various platforms, including Turkish non-governmental organizations and charitable institutions providing basic goods and services to communities in need. The agreement was signed in Antalya, Türkiye, on the sidelines of the COP31 United Nations climate conference by Somalia's Minister of Family and Human Rights Development, Khadija Mohamed Al-Makhzoumi, and Türkiye's Minister of Family and Social Services, Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş. advertisements According to Somalia's Ministry of Family and Human Rights Development, the agreement establishes a framework for cooperation in developing social welfare policies, exchanging expertise and strengthening services for vulnerable communities. It also provides for cooperation in improving health and education services, along with care and rehabilitation programs for persons with disabilities and older people. The two governments agreed to organize training programs, conferences and seminars to strengthen the skills of social service professionals and facilitate the exchange of knowledge and experience. “The agreement is an important step toward improving Somalia's social services,” Al-Makhzoumi added, saying the government hopes to benefit from the experience of international partners, particularly Türkiye, in strengthening family protection and safeguarding the rights of women and children. The Somali minister also addressed a side event at COP31 focusing on the relationship between climate change, social protection and women's empowerment. She said recurring droughts and floods have severely affected Somali families, particularly women and children, who face increasing hardship as climate-related disasters disrupt livelihoods and access to essential services. Al-Makhzoumi called for international climate financing to reach the most vulnerable communities, especially rural families disproportionately affected by droughts and flooding. She also emphasized the importance of including women in the development of climate policies and adaptation strategies, highlighting their role in strengthening community resilience. The agreement comes as Somalia seeks greater international cooperation to improve social services and expand protection for communities affected by humanitarian emergencies and climate-related disasters. Türkiye has been one of Somalia's closest international partners since President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan visited Mogadishu in 2011 during a devastating drought and famine. Since then, Ankara has provided humanitarian assistance and supported projects in education, healthcare, infrastructure and institutional development. The two countries have also expanded cooperation in defense, military training, maritime security and energy development. The latest agreement broadens that relationship by placing greater emphasis on social welfare, family protection and support for vulnerable populations. (AP Photo/Abdel Kareem Hana) Mogadishu (HOL) — Somalia has joined 17 other Arab and Islamic countries in condemning an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in southern Gaza, urging Israel to uphold the ceasefire, protect civilians and allow unrestricted humanitarian assistance into the Palestinian territory. In a joint statement issued Saturday, Nov. 14, the foreign ministers of the 18 countries said the strike on the hospital in Khan Younis caused casualties among patients and medical personnel and violated international humanitarian law, which provides special protection for healthcare facilities and workers. advertisements The statement was signed by the foreign ministers of Somalia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Egypt, Jordan, Sudan, Libya, Palestine, Djibouti, Algeria, Lebanon, Mauritania, Türkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia. The ministers also condemned continued Israeli attacks on Palestinian civilians, including strikes on tents and other shelters housing displaced families. They warned that the attacks threaten the Gaza ceasefire and undermine international efforts to restore security and stability in the territory. The joint statement expressed serious concern over Israeli restrictions on humanitarian assistance, including essential medical supplies and shelter materials such as tents, caravans and mobile homes. The ministers said the restrictions were worsening Gaza's humanitarian crisis as winter approaches, leaving displaced families exposed to harsh weather conditions. They warned that inadequate shelter, deteriorating sanitation facilities and limited access to clean water and healthcare were placing civilians at serious risk, particularly children and infants. The foreign ministers called on Israel to immediately and fully implement its commitments under the Sharm el-Sheikh agreement, U.S. President Donald Trump's comprehensive peace plan and United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803 of 2025. They urged Israel to maintain the ceasefire, protect civilians and medical facilities, and ensure the safe, sustained and unrestricted delivery of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities. The statement also called for the entry of equipment and supplies needed to restore essential infrastructure and support early recovery efforts in Gaza. The ministers emphasized that humanitarian assistance should not be delayed by political or security conditions or made dependent on progress in subsequent phases of the peace agreement. “We call on Israel to allow United Nations agencies and humanitarian organizations to carry out their operations without obstruction,” they added. The countries urged the United States and the Board of Peace to intensify diplomatic efforts to ensure Israel fulfills its commitments and removes restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza. الإسماعيلية المصرية (winwin) 14 نوفمبر 2026 خاص | المريخ السوداني يحسم ملفات مهمة قبل الاستئناف المريخ الدوري السوداني الممتاز كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin يواصل فريق المريخ الأول والرديف تحضيراتهما لاستئناف منافسات الدوري الرواندي والنسخة الجديدة من الدوري الممتاز السوداني، وذلك بعد فترة التوقف الدولي التي جاءت في توقيت مناسب، عقب الإقصاء من الدور التمهيدي الثاني لدوري أبطال أفريقيا. ويستعد الفريق الرديف للعودة إلى البلاد للمشاركة في النسخة 31 من الدوري الممتاز، عقب اختتام معسكر ناجح بمدينة الإسماعيلية المصرية، خاض خلاله عددا مقدرا من المباريات التجريبية. روموالد راكوتوندربي يقود المريخ في الممتاز نفى عضو بارز في إدارة نادي المريخ، فضل حجب اسمه، في حديث خاص لموقع "winwin"، كل ما تردد بشأن نية الإدارة إسناد مهمة تدريب الفريق الأول إلى المدرب روموالد راكوتوندربي، والتعاقد مع مدرب محلي لقيادة الفريق الرديف. وأكد المصدر استمرار المدرب الملغاشي في منصبه، وإشرافه على الفريق الرديف في مباريات الدوري الممتاز، مشيرا إلى استمرار جندي نميري في قيادة الفريق الأول بالدوري الرواندي بتكليف من الإدارة. اقرأ أيضًا: مهددًا بالتصعيد لـ"كاس".. المريخ يربك اتحاد الكرة السوداني الهلال يستعيد لقب الدوري ويقصي المريخ من السباق العربي وشدد المتحدث على أن الإدارة حددت أهداف مشاركتها في المسابقة الرواندية، معربا عن ثقته في المدرب المحلي، إلى حين التعاقد مع مدير فني أجنبي، بناء على توصية المدير الرياضي الذي تجري مشاورات حاليا للتعاقد معه. winwin يكشف موعد عودة المريخ إلى السودان وأكد المصدر أن إدارة النادي حددت يوم الجمعة المقبل، الموافق 20 نوفمبر/تشرين الثاني، موعدا لعودة الفريق الرديف إلى السودان، استعدادا للمشاركة في المرحلة الأولى من النسخة 31 لمسابقة الدوري الممتاز، بقيادة المدرب الملغاشي روموالد راكوتوندربي. وسيفتتح الفريق مشواره في البطولة ضمن مجموعة العاصمة الخرطوم، بمواجهة فريق كوبر يوم 25 من الشهر ذاته. وختم المصدر حديثه بالتأكيد أن إدارة النادي فضلت التريث في اختيار المدير الرياضي والمدرب الأجنبي، تجنبا للتسرع في اتخاذ قرارات مهمة، مشيرا إلى أنها وضعت خططا عاجلة لضمان ظهور قوي للفريق في الدوريين الرواندي والسوداني، إلى جانب خطط مستقبلية تهدف إلى إعادة
